statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with circumcenter $O$. Points $D, E, F$ lie in the interiors of sides $BC, CA, AB$ respectively, with $DE \perp CO$ and $DF \perp BO$. Let $K$ be the circumcenter of $\triangle AFE$. Prove that $DK \perp BC$.

Find the greatest possible integer $m$ (in terms of $n$) such that a table with $m$ rows and $n$ columns can be filled with real numbers so that for any two different rows $[a_1,\ldots,a_n]$ and $[b_1,\ldots,b_n]$, $\max_i |a_i - b_i| = 1$.
Find all functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f(yf(x+y) + f(x)) = 4x + 2yf(x+y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$.

A set $A$ of integers is \textit{sum-full} if $A \subseteq A + A$ (every element is a sum of two elements of $A$). A set $A$ is \textit{zero-sum-free} if $0$ is the only integer not expressible as a sum of elements of a finite nonempty subset of $A$. Does there exist a sum-full zero-sum-free set of integers?
Primes $p$ and $q$ satisfy $\dfrac{p}{p+1} + \dfrac{q+1}{q} = \dfrac{2n}{n+2}$ for some positive integer $n$. Find all possible values of $q - p$.

On Mugbook, each of infinitely many people has finitely many friends, and each person designates one friend as their best friend. Someone is a $k$-best friend if they are the best friend of an $(k-1)$-best friend; a person is 	extit{popular} if they are a $k$-best friend for every $k$.

(a) Prove every popular person is the best friend of a popular person.

(b) Show that if people can have infinitely many friends, a popular person may not be the best friend of a popular person.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be acute-angled with circumcircle $\Gamma$ and orthocenter $H$. Let $K \in \Gamma$ be on the opposite side of $BC$ from $A$. Let $L$ be the reflection of $K$ in $AB$, and $M$ the reflection of $K$ in $BC$. Let $E$ be the second intersection of $\Gamma$ with the circumcircle of $\triangle BLM$. Show that $KH$, $EM$, $BC$ are concurrent.
A word is \textit{repetitive} if it is a concatenation of at least two identical subwords. Prove that if swapping any two adjacent letters makes a word repetitive, then all its letters are identical.
